look_here_first: If a female tree has cones, start there: eastern redcedar has small glaucous blue-black cones about 4.5–5 mm across, commonly with 1–2(–3) seeds. Then inspect an adult scale leaf: the resin gland is pit-like/depressed near the base rather than a raised rounded mid-blade gland. Ashe juniper usually has larger 6.5–9.6 mm cones with one seed and a raised circular-to-hemispheric gland.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Evergreen dioecious small to medium tree, often single-trunked and conic/columnar when young.

key_traits.label: Bark
key_traits.text: Red-brown bark exfoliating or shredding in thin strips.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Adult leaves tiny and appressed in four-ranked sprays; resin gland pit-like/depressed near the basal-central part of the scale. Vigorous shoots can bear longer awl-shaped leaves.

key_traits.label: Reproductive
key_traits.text: Mature seed cones berrylike, glaucous blue-black, about 4.5–5 mm and commonly 1–2(–3)-seeded.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: evergreen dioecious small to medium tree, often with a single trunk and conic/columnar crown when young

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: adult foliage shoots slender, approximately four-sided, with closely appressed opposite scale leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: adult scale leaves about 1 mm long, dark green and often slightly glossy

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: resin gland expressed as a small pit/depression near the basal-central part of the scale leaf

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: vigorous juvenile/whip shoots may carry longer sharp awl-shaped leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: bark red-brown, thin and exfoliating/shredding in strips

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mature berrylike seed cones small, about 4.5–5 mm, glaucous blue-black

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: seed cones commonly 1–2(–3)-seeded, often with one seed larger

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: more associated with Blackland Prairie/Post Oak/eastern or mesic sites than the dry limestone cedar-break dominance of Ashe juniper
